Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Happy to outline the short answers and follow up with a more detailed breakdown once we see your exact traffic distribution. Short answers: 

- We bill scoring primarily per candidate evaluated ("per-scoring-unit") for rerank endpoints; classifier passes that evaluate candidates are treated as scoring units.
- Token-based compute is used under the hood for model selection and runtime accounting; large differences in candidate length can change CPU/GPU cost but we expose the per-scoring-unit price to simplify budgeting.
- Batching reduces per-token overhead and can lower your effective cost; we recommend configuring batch-size to match your P95 latency SLO.
- We offer volume tier discounts and a committed capacity path (Dedicated) if you want predictable unit economics at 100k+/day.

I'll have Aditya follow with a sample rate card and a monthly estimate based on the numbers you sent. Can you confirm if 8 candidates is the upper-bound or the average? Also let me know if you plan to run multi-stage classification (i.e., a lightweight filter + heavyweight reranker) as that changes the mix of scoring units.

Hi Oliver — jumping in with a concrete breakdown and an attached rate card (see Rerank_Ratecard_v3.xlsx). I kept the math simple so your procurement team can plug numbers quickly. Key points up front: 

1) Unit definitions (what you will see on the invoice)
- Scoring unit (SU): one classifier or reranker evaluation on one candidate. If you run a classifier on 8 candidates, that counts as 8 SUs. If you then rerank top-5 with a model that scores pairs, rerank cost is counted as 5 SUs.
- Token compute: under the hood we measure tokens for runtime telemetry and to decide kernel selection; token usage influences cost tiers for very long candidates but does not change the SU price for typical candidate lengths (<64 tokens).

2) Baseline list prices (hosted API, non-committed)
- Classifier SU: $0.00045 per SU
- Reranker SU: $0.00070 per SU
- Embedding/aux calls: priced separately as per standard API (not included here)

3) Effective per-query math (your average profile: 8 candidates -> classifier on 8, rerank top-5):
- Classifier cost: 8 * $0.00045 = $0.00360 per query
- Reranker cost: 5 * $0.00070 = $0.00350 per query
- Total per-query (baseline): $0.00710
- Daily @100k queries: $710/day -> ~$21,300/month (30-day) at list rates

4) Batching and latency trade-offs
- If you batch candidates in a single request (send the 8 candidates together), the platform can amortize per-request overhead and reduce the effective SU cost by ~8-15% depending on model/kernel path. For long candidates (>128 tokens) the savings shrink.
- For your 6-token candidate average, expect closer to 12% savings at 8-way batching. I showed a worked example in the spreadsheet.

5) Two-stage flow impact
- The cheap rule filter is free (client-side). The classifier SUs apply to all surviving candidates. If you can filter down to 4 candidates on average, that cuts classifier spend by ~50%.

6) Discounting and committed pricing
- Sustained volume discount: 10% off list for monthly spend > $10k, 18% for > $50k, and deeper Dedicated/reserved pricing available for > $100k/month (custom SLA + capacity).
- We can provide a 60-day evaluation credit to validate the effective cost with your real traffic (I can include credit in the proposal).

7) Next steps
- I attached a sample monthly estimate and the XLSX ratecard. If you share a 2-week request log (IDs + candidate counts), I can run a more precise estimate and flag any outliers that might push you into token-tier pricing.
